prerequisites: Knowledge of technical and industrial drafting standards.
Ability to extract from a technical drawing geometric, functional and technological information.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the theoretical knowledge required to select the most appropriate geometric modelling strategy for a given mechanical assembly.
Acquire practical skills needed to effectively use feature-based parametric solid modelling software.
Systematic knowledge of the key aspects of mechanical design in industrial engineering and the related methodologies.

Understand the most appropriate methods for defining a product and its characteristics. The study of mechanical components and assemblies, their basic sizing, and their graphical representation constitutes the main area of knowledge and understanding.

Understanding of the broader multidisciplinary context of engineering, with particular emphasis on problem-solving approaches that start from the identification of a problem, investigate its causes, and identify appropriate multidisciplinary solutions.
Knowledge of information technologies and their role in supporting engineering design activities.
Knowledge of the most appropriate manufacturing processes for the production of mechanical components.

Ability to select and apply appropriate analytical, modelling, and verification methods for the design and analysis of machines and mechanical systems, including the interpretation and production of detail and assembly drawings using CAD software, as well as the functional design of mechanical systems by applying the principles of kinematics, kinetostatics, statics, and dynamics.

Ability to select and use appropriate tools, equipment, and methods for the design and production of products and services, with particular reference to three-dimensional CAD modelling software and technical information management systems.
Ability to combine theoretical knowledge and practical skills in order to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems.
Ability to select the most appropriate manufacturing process for the production of mechanical components.
Ability to analyse data and information using established methods and tools, interpret results, and draw consistent conclusions, also with the support of provided guidance.
Ability to compare alternative engineering solutions and contribute to technically justified decisions by referring to engineering standards and established industrial procedures.
Ability to work collaboratively and effectively within a team, understanding the engineering context of a problem and recognizing the main interdisciplinary implications of the application domain.

Ability to organize one's work while meeting assigned deadlines, managing available time and resources effectively, realistically assessing one's own capabilities, and contributing to task prioritization.
Ability to recognize personal knowledge limitations and the need to acquire new competencies by identifying appropriate information sources and guided learning opportunities.

Ability to communicate and convey information, ideas, problems, and solutions in engineering contexts to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, using appropriate technical language and referring to familiar application scenarios.
Ability to present engineering problems, solutions, analyses, and results clearly and systematically through written reports and oral presentations, following standard formats and conventions.

Ability to graphically represent and communicate technical data, results, and engineering solutions through the preparation of technical drawings, diagrams, graphs, and tables, using established tools and conventions.
Ability to acquire and update knowledge in the relevant engineering field, independently, although primarily under guidance, by using established educational resources and learning tools.

Ability to identify and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation through the main available resources (libraries, databases, technical manuals, and digital resources), selecting relevant information with appropriate guidance.

Ability to learn through project-based and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) methodologies by applying acquired knowledge and engineering tools to case studies and real-world engineering problems of appropriate complexity.

syllabus_topics: The product development process
CAD/CAE systems supporting the design process
CAD as a common tool for design and fabrication
Tools and techniques for virtual prototyping
CAD software packages requirements for Mechanical Design
Features of currently available CAD software packages and choice criteria
3D modelling of solid bodies and surface bodies
Modeling strategies and design intent
Parametric modeling: parametric and variational approaches
Modeling constraints: geometric, dimensional and algebraic
2D sketch: basic functions, associativity, automatic, geometric and dimensional constraints
2D Sketch and its functions
3D Sketch and its functions
Support geometry: planes, axes and points
The spline function
3D functions from sketch: base extrusion, cut extrusion, etc.
3D direct functions: chamfer, fillet, mirror, etc.
Creation and management of configurations (either manually or by design tables)
Assembly procedures: bottom-up and top-down
Assembly functions
Annotations, GD&T
Toolbox: use of libraries to insert commercial parts into the model/drawing
Surface modeling and use of surfaces into the solid modeler
The Finite Element Method (hints)

assessment_methods.method: Final Oral Exam (machine/device design and discussion)
Open questions about basic concepts and IT techniques

assessment_rules: The final oral exam involves the creation and discussion of a machine/device design using 3D CAD software, followed by open questions on basic concepts and IT techniques. Students must demonstrate good knowledge of basic 3D modelling approaches, proficiency in 3D and 2D CAD tools, and sufficient knowledge of technical representation standards and GD&T annotation systems. Grading ranges from Fail (insufficient) to 29-30 and Honors (Excellent or outstanding), based on conceptual understanding, application ability, independence, critical thinking, and communication. Honors are awarded for brilliance and originality exceeding expectations.
